newsitem.title: USA: Most US Eurodollar futures end short day unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Most US Eurodollar futures end short day unchanged.

text.p: U.S. Eurodollar futures closed an abbreviated session unchanged, as even the upcoming Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting on Wednesday failed to spark any interest in the light U.S. holiday session, analysts said.
They said the market is anticipating that the FOMC will leave U.S. monetary policy unchanged.

Key U.S. inflationary data this week should also keep Eurodollars pinned within ranges. Neither the U.S. Producer Price Index (PPI) on Wednesday nor Thursday's Consumer Price Index (CPI) should send March EDH7 climbing much above the 94.50 level, analysts said.
October PPI is seen rising 0.2 percent overall and 0.1 percent in the core rate, while the October CPI is forecast to increase 0.3 percent overall and 0.2 percent excluding food and energy.
Retail sales for October, which will also be released on Thursday, are forecast to gain 0.3 percent overall and in the core rate.

Two weekly chain store sales reports, the Mitsubishi Chain Store survy and Redbook, will be released on Tuesday, and could give the market short-term guidance when it resumes regularly scheduled trade.

U.S. bond futures are expected to open Tuesday higher after December set eight-month highs last week. Positive technical factors could lead December to 114-18/32, which is the 62-percent Fibonacci retracement level from the contract's January to July decline.

Bond futures will be traded in Monday's night pit session and overnight on Project A after being shut all day. Eurodollars will trade on GLOBEX on Monday night after closing pit trade at 1200 CST/1800 GMT due to U.S. Veterans Day.
March and June Eurodolllars were unchanged at the end of pit trade at 94.45 and 94.35, respectively.
